Messages.Author: Kalessin
Messages.Body:
Yesterday a doubt arised during gameplay.

Selena (4-5 blood on her) was in combat with a !Malk (5 blood on
him/her), the !Malk being the acting minion.

Selena played Thoughts betrayed at inferior (bad move, granted), her
player believing his opponent had no Coma in his hand. Well it turned
out he did have one, and the !malk played it, paying all 3 blood for
it. As a response, Selena played a theft of vitae.

Thus, the question is: the !malk goes to torpor (he spends 3 blood on
the Coma, gets his two remaining blood stolen and then suffers an
additional damage from the TB), or he just gets first the damage from
the TB at inferior and THEN gets stealed the remaining blood?

Thanks in advance!
Andrés Valenzuela

Messages.Author: Emmit Svenson
Messages.Body:
Kalessin wrote:
> Selena (4-5 blood on her) was in combat with a !Malk (5 blood on
> him/her), the !Malk being the acting minion.
>
> Selena played Thoughts betrayed at inferior (bad move, granted), her
> player believing his opponent had no Coma in his hand. Well it turned
> out he did have one, and the !malk played it, paying all 3 blood for
> it. As a response, Selena played a theft of vitae.
>
> Thus, the question is: the !malk goes to torpor (he spends 3 blood on
> the Coma, gets his two remaining blood stolen and then suffers an
> additional damage from the TB), or he just gets first the damage from
> the TB at inferior and THEN gets stealed the remaining blood?

Strike resolution happens before damage handling, so the blood gets
thefted before the !Malk can use it to heal damage. He ends up in
torpor.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1133103587.5...@g44g2000cwa.googlegroups.com>,

Emmit Svenson <emmits...@hotmail.com> writes:
>Strike resolution happens before damage handling, so the blood gets
>thefted before the !Malk can use it to heal damage.

Damage handling is part of strike resolution. However, it's handled
after the effects of other strikes are applied.

For clarification, see 6.4.3, Resolve Strike.
